title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Elasticity — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Define stress, strain, and Young's modulus. What are their SI units?
questions.solution:
**Stress** = deforming force per unit area (F/A). SI unit: **pascal (Pa)**.

**Strain** = fractional change in dimension (ΔL/L). SI unit: **none (dimensionless)**.

**Young's modulus** = stress/strain within the elastic limit. SI unit: **pascal (Pa)**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Three moduli: Young's (tensile), shear/rigidity (shape), bulk (volume). Steel's Y ≈ 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.question: A steel wire of cross-sectional area 2 mm² is stretched by a 100 N force. Calculate the stress. If Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, what is the strain?
questions.knowledgeNote: Convert mm² to m² (×10⁻⁶) before dividing — the commonest unit slip in this unit.

questions.question: State Hooke's law. A 2 m wire extends by 2 mm under a 50 N load. Calculate the force constant of the wire.
questions.solution:
**Hooke's law:** within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain (extension ∝ load for a wire).

Force constant k = F/x = 50/(2 × 10⁻³) = **25,000 N/m**.
questions.knowledgeNote: k = YA/L for a wire — thicker and shorter wires are stiffer.

questions.question: How much energy is stored in the wire of the previous question when stretched by the 50 N load?
questions.solution:
Elastic potential energy U = ½Fx = ½kx².

U = ½ × 50 × (2 × 10⁻³) = **0.05 J**.

(Equivalently ½ × 25,000 × (2 × 10⁻³)² = 0.05 J.)
questions.knowledgeNote: This is the area under the force–extension graph — the same ½Fx triangle as the spring.

questions.question: Define bulk modulus and Poisson's ratio. Why is Poisson's ratio dimensionless?
questions.solution:
**Bulk modulus** B = −V(ΔP/ΔV): resistance to uniform compression.

**Poisson's ratio** σ = lateral strain / longitudinal strain: how much a stretched body thins sideways.

Both strains are ratios of lengths, so their quotient has **no units** — it is a pure number (between 0 and 0.5 for most materials).
questions.knowledgeNote: Rubber ≈ 0.5 (volume conserved), cork ≈ 0 — cork is why wine stoppers slide in without bulging.

questions.question: A steel cable of cross-sectional area 5 mm² has a breaking stress of 8 × 10⁸ Pa. What maximum mass can it lift? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
Maximum force = breaking stress × area = (8 × 10⁸) × (5 × 10⁻⁶) = 4000 N.

m = F/g = 4000/10 = **400 kg**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Real cables use a safety factor (working stress ≈ breaking stress / 5–10) — NEB sometimes asks for it as a follow-up.
